subject: General Studies
question: Who among the following has been awarded as the 'Best actor' (male) at the BRICS film festival 2021?
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Dhanush won Best Actor (Male) at the BRICS Film Festival 2021 for 'Asuran'. Nawazuddin, Akshay Kumar, and Pankaj Tripathi were strong names in Indian cinema that year but did not take this particular award.

subject: General Studies
question: Who is the first Indian Physicist to win the Prestigious Boltzmann Medal for the year 2022?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Professor Deepak Dhar became the first Indian physicist to receive the Boltzmann Medal in 2022, awarded by IUPAP for outstanding contributions to statistical physics. Ashok Kumar Barua, Bimla Buti, and D.D. Bhawalkar are respected physicists but not Boltzmann Medal winners.

subject: General Studies
question: Who is the First Indian Woman to win two medals in the Tokyo 2020 (held in Aug-Sep 2021) Paralympics Games?
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Avani Lekhara became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympic medals at Tokyo 2020 — gold in 10m air rifle SH1 and bronze in 50m rifle 3 positions SH1. Bhavina Patel also shone in table tennis but did not double-medal.

subject: General Studies
question: As per Report 2021 of Global Observatory on Donation and Transplantation (GODT), India has been ranked _______ in Organ donation and transplantation in World.
explanation: On this one, option C is correct. The Global Observatory on Donation and Transplantation (GODT) Report 2021 placed India third in the world for organ donation and transplantation activity. First and second are typically taken by leading Western and East Asian programmes — fifth is too low for India's volume.

subject: General Studies
question: Which Credit Scheme is launched for Prisoners of Yerwada Central Jail in 2022 as a Pilot Scheme?
explanation: The right pick is option D. Bank of Maharashtra launched 'Jivhala' as a pilot credit scheme for inmates of Yerwada Central Jail in 2022, helping them access formal banking on release. Sahanubhuti, Aage Badho, and Bank for Prisoners are distractors from other welfare contexts.

subject: General Studies
question: Who is the author of the book, 'Beyond Possible'?
explanation: Go with option B. 'Beyond Possible' is the memoir of Nimsdai Purja, the Nepalese-British mountaineer who climbed all fourteen 8000-metre peaks in record time. Bernadette McDonald, Arunima Sinha, and Stephen Alter have written on mountains and adventure but not under this title.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following option is associated with Amrit Sarovar Mission?
explanation: Pick option A. Mission Amrit Sarovar aims to develop and rejuvenate at least 75 water bodies in every district — a water-conservation push tied to Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav. Soil conservation, air pollution, and fishery are separate government agendas.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following statements are correct about the 'Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra Yojana'? (a) This scheme is initiated by Delhi government in 2018. (b) Any citizen of India can avail this scheme. (c) Ayodhya is recently included in the list of places that one can visit under this scheme.
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Delhi's Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra Yojana started in 2018 and later added Ayodhya to its pilgrimage list — so (a) and (c) hold. Statement (b) is incorrect because the scheme is for eligible Delhi residents, not any citizen of India.

subject: General Studies
question: Rajiv Gandhi Orang National Park, which has been renamed as Orang National Park, is located in which Indian State?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Orang National Park — earlier Rajiv Gandhi Orang National Park — sits on the north bank of the Brahmaputra in Assam and is often called the 'Mini Kaziranga'. Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Uttarakhand host other famous parks but not Orang.

subject: General Studies
question: Select the correct statement/s - (India - Central Asia Summit) (a) The First India - Central Asia Summit held in January, 2022 (b) Republic of Tajikistan, Republic of Uzbekistan were present for the Summit.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. The first India–Central Asia Summit was held virtually in January 2022, with leaders including the Presidents of Tajikistan and Uzbekistan among the five Central Asian republics invited. Both statements in the stem are therefore correct.

subject: Economy
question: Who has been appointed as a new Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog in May 2022?
explanation: The right pick is option D. Suman K. Bery was appointed Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog in May 2022, succeeding Rajiv Kumar. Ramesh Chand served as NITI member-agriculture; Jayati Ghosh and Rajiv Kumar held other roles but not this May 2022 vice-chair appointment.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following Organisation is organising a special programme for school children called 'Young Scientist Programme' 'Yuva Vigyani Karyakram' 'YUVIKA'?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. ISRO runs YUVIKA — Yuva Vigyani Karyakram — a residential programme to groom school students in space science. UNICEF, BARC, and DRDO run youth or research initiatives but not this specific Young Scientist Programme.

subject: General Studies
question: 'Remove laws that harm, create laws that empower' is the theme of which day?
explanation: On this one, option A is correct. Zero Discrimination Day (1 March), observed by UNAIDS, carried the theme 'Remove laws that harm, create laws that empower'. World AIDS Day, World Equality Day, and World Social Justice Day use different annual themes.

subject: General Studies
question: _______ has been appointed as the chairman of the ISRO, the Indian Space Research Institute in January, 2022.
explanation: Go with option B. Dr S. Somnath took over as ISRO Chairman in January 2022, replacing Dr K. Sivan. Radhakrishnan and Prof. MGK Menon were earlier chairmen — useful timeline anchors when MPSC asks 'who in January 2022'.

subject: Reasoning
question: Which operation was launched by Punjab's Excise Department in 2020 to curb illicit liquor trading related crimes?
explanation: Pick option B. Punjab's Excise Department launched Operation Red Rose in 2020 to crack down on illicit liquor trade and related crime. Black Cobra, Black Bull, and Prahar sound plausible but belong to other enforcement drives in different states or years.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following amendments imposed restrictions on the Fundamental Rights of the citizens to protect the sovereignty and integrity of the country?
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. The 16th Amendment (1963) added 'the sovereignty and integrity of India' as a ground to restrict freedoms under Article 19, tightening limits on speech and association. The 14th, 24th, and 39th Amendments dealt with citizenship, property, and emergency-era changes — not this specific restriction.

subject: General Studies
question: In which year the British accepted the demand for making the constituent assembly of India?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. The August Offer of 1940 was the first time the British formally accepted the principle of a constituent assembly for framing India's constitution. 1938–39 saw Congress demands but no acceptance; 1942 brought the Quit India movement, not this concession.

subject: Polity
question: What are all the nine Articles covered under Part XVII of the Constitution?
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Part XVII of the Constitution covers the Official Language and runs from Article 343 to Article 351 — nine articles in all. The other ranges either spill into Part XVI on special provisions or start Part XVIII on emergency provisions.

subject: Polity
question: According to the article 154 of the Indian Constitution executive power of State is vested in the hands of _______.
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Governor, who exercises it either directly or through officers subordinate to him. The Chief Minister and Council of Ministers aid and advise the Governor — they do not hold the constitutional vesting clause.

subject: General Studies
question: _______ round-table conferences were held in London from 1930 to 1932 to see how best Indians could administer their country.
explanation: The right pick is option C. Three Round Table Conferences met in London between 1930 and 1932 to discuss constitutional reform and Indian self-government under the Simon Commission aftermath. Two or four conferences is a common count trap — memorise 'three' for MPSC chronology.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the following: (a) Habeas-corpus → (i) To transfer a case from lower to higher court (b) Mandamus → (ii) To look into legality of a post (c) Quo warranto → (iii) To command authority to Perform its duty (d) Certiorari → (iv) To look into legality of arrest
explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Match the pairs: Habeas corpus checks the legality of detention — (iv); Mandamus commands a public authority to perform its duty — (iii); Quo warranto questions the legality of holding a public office — (ii); Certiorari transfers a case up or quashes a lower court's order — (i).

subject: Polity
question: According to article 243 E of the Indian Constitution every gram panchayat unless dissolved earlier under any law for the time being in force, shall continue for five years from _______.

options.A: the date of declaration of election results
options.B: the date of declaration of election
options.C: the date appointed for its first meeting after elections
options.D: the beginning of first financial year after the Panchayat elections

explanation: Go with option C. Article 243E fixes the five-year term of a gram panchayat from the date appointed for its first meeting after elections — not from result declaration, poll day, or the next financial year. That first-meeting date is the statutory starting point.

subject: General Studies
question: Fundamental duties were included on the recommendation of which Committee?
explanation: Pick option C. The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended inserting Fundamental Duties, which the 42nd Amendment added as Part IVA Article 51A. Devraj, Karan Singh, and Kripalani committees touched other constitutional reforms but not this list.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following is not the functions of Gram Sevak?

options.A: Proper utilization of Gram Panchayat Funds
options.C: Collection of Various Taxes prescribed by the Government

explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Gram Sevaks routinely handle panchayat fund use, gram sabha reporting, and government-prescribed tax collection — all three listed items are standard duties. Since none of A, B, or C is a 'non-function', 'None of these' is the correct choice.

subject: Polity
question: By which Amendment the 11th Fundamental Duty was later added to the list? (51A(K))
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. The 11th Fundamental Duty — Article 51A(k), making parents/guardians provide education to children aged 6–14 — came through the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. The 42nd Amendment added the original ten duties in 1976; 52nd and 62nd dealt with anti-defection and reservation tenure.

subject: General Studies
question: Identify the person based on the following description: (a) First Journalist in Marathi (b) The teacher of Prince of Akkalkot (c) Founder of Marathi Newspapers (d) Director of Colaba Weather Observatory
explanation: The right pick is option C. Balshastri Jambhekar edited the first Marathi newspaper Darpan, taught the Akkalkot prince, launched early Marathi journalism, and headed the Colaba Observatory — all four clues fit one name.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following statements are true about Narayan Meghaji Lokhande? (a) Founder of Labour Movement (b) Establishment of Bombay mill hands Association in 1884 (c) 'Raobahadur' award by the British Government (d) Establishment of Maharashtra Labour Union
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Narayan Meghaji Lokhande is remembered as a pioneer of the Bombay labour movement, he helped set up the Bombay Mill-Hands' Association (1884), and the British honoured him with the title 'Raobahadur' — statements (a), (b) and (c) stand. The Maharashtra Labour Union came much later and is not his work, so (d) drops out.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the following: (a) Rand and Ayerst's Murder → (i) V.D. Savarkar (b) Abhinav Bharat → (ii) Anant Laxman Kanhere (c) Justice Jackson's Murder → (iii) Madan Lal Dhingra (d) Curzon Wyllies Murder → (iv) Chaphekar Brothers
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Pair each incident with its actor: Rand and Ayerst (Chapekar brothers), Abhinav Bharat (Savarkar), Justice Jackson (Anant Laxman Kanhere), Curzon Wyllie (Madan Lal Dhingra) — sequence (iv), (i), (ii), (iii).

subject: History
question: In which Session of National Congress the two groups came together again?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. After the 1907 Surat split, Moderates and Extremists reunited at the Lucknow Session of 1916 under the joint leadership of Tilak and Annie Besant.

subject: History
question: Who was the Chairman of first All Bengal Students Council held in 1928?
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. The inaugural All Bengal Students' Conference in September 1928 was presided over by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru; Pramod Kumar Ghoshal became president of the association itself, not chairman of that opening session.

subject: General Studies
question: Name the Social Reformer who got married to a Widow?
explanation: On this one, option D is correct. Maharshi Dhondo Keshav Karve married a widow in 1893 and made widow remarriage a lived example of his social-reform mission — the other names are reformers but not remembered chiefly for this act.

subject: General Studies
question: Who was the first Indian Lady, who received Degree in Medical Science in America?
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Anandibai Joshi graduated from the Women's Medical College of Pennsylvania in 1886 — the first Indian woman to earn a medical degree in America.

subject: General Studies
question: Deindustrialization of India in British Period means: (a) Decline of Handicraft Industry in India (b) Decline of Cottage Industry (c) Development in rural life (d) Development in agriculture
explanation: Go with option A. 'Deindustrialisation' under British rule chiefly means the ruin of Indian handicrafts and cottage industries through factory competition and one-way trade — not rural uplift or agricultural 'development' in the positive sense.

subject: History
question: Match the following: Revolt Centre → Leadership (a) Kolhapur → (i) Appasaheb Patvardhan (b) Jamkhandi → (ii) Chimasaheb (c) Aurangabad → (iii) Babasaheb Bhave (d) Nargund → (iv) Phida Ali
explanation: Pick option B. Per the official answer, the 1857 revolt centres map as Kolhapur–Chimasaheb, Jamkhandi–Appasaheb Patvardhan, Aurangabad–Phida Ali, Nargund–Babasaheb Bhave — code (ii), (i), (iv), (iii). Match from the list the paper gave rather than reshuffling from memory.

subject: Reasoning
question: Which of the following programmes were started by Mahatma Gandhi with Non-cooperation Movement? (a) To Propagate Swadeshi (b) Hindu - Muslim Unity (c) Prohibition of liquor (d) Removal of Untouchability
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Gandhi linked the Non-cooperation Movement with swadeshi propaganda, Hindu–Muslim unity, liquor prohibition, and the fight against untouchability — all four programmes were on his agenda.

subject: History
question: Where was the first Revolt of the Peasants occured on 12th May, 1875?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. The Deccan agrarian disturbances of 1875 began on 12 May at Supe (Supa) in Pune district when peasants attacked moneylenders' shops and debt bonds — the spark for the wider riots.

subject: General Studies
question: Which Commission was appointed by the Bombay Government to inquire into the on going Peasant discontent in the South?
explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Alarmed by peasant violence in the Deccan, the Bombay Government appointed the Deccan Riots Commission (1876) to probe the causes of the 1875 disturbances.

subject: Polity
question: Who was the President of 'Asprushyata Nivarak Parishad' held in Mumbai in 1918?
explanation: Go with option C. Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde organised the Asprushyata Nivarak Parishad at Bombay in March 1918 and Maharaja Sayajirao Gaikwad presided over the session.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following Famous Personalities were produced by 'Bharat Sevak Samaj'? (a) Shrinivas Shastri (b) Pandit Hridaynath Kunjru, Thakkarbappa (c) N.M. Joshi, Kakasaheb Limaye (d) Vishnushastri Chiplunkar, Keshavrao Bagde
explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Bharat Sevak Samaj (1915) nurtured social workers such as Shrinivas Shastri, Hridaynath Kunjru and Thakkarbappa, and trade-union figures like N.M. Joshi and Kakasaheb Limaye — not Chiplunkar or Bagde.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following state has more geographical area?
explanation: Pick option A. Rajasthan covers about 3.42 lakh sq km — the largest state by geographical area among the four listed; Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh all rank below it.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following State Shares its boundary with two Countries?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Mizoram shares international borders with Bangladesh and Myanmar — two countries; Tripura, Manipur and Nagaland each touch only one foreign neighbour in this set.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the following: Iron and Steel Industry → State (a) Bokaro → (i) Karnataka (b) Durgapur → (ii) Odisha (c) Rourkela → (iii) West Bengal (d) Bhadrawati → (iv) Bihar
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Bokaro lies in Bihar (now Jharkhand), Durgapur in West Bengal, Rourkela in Odisha, and Bhadrawati in Karnataka — sequence (iv), (iii), (ii), (i).

subject: Geography
question: As per Census 2011, which of the following district has high sex-ratio?
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Census 2011 placed Satara among the higher sex-ratio districts of Maharashtra — well above Aurangabad, Buldhana and Jalgaon in that comparison.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following is the correct descending order of mountain peaks according to their heights in Maharashtra?
explanation: The right pick is option A. Kalsubai (1646 m) tops Maharashtra, followed by Salher, then Mahabaleshwar and Trimbakeshwar in descending height — the order the key expects.

subject: Geography
question: Match the correct pairs of Hot water spring and its locational districts in Maharashtra: (a) Salbardi → (i) Jalgaon (b) Sav → (ii) Thane (c) Vajreshwari → (iii) Raigad (d) Changdev → (iv) Amaravati
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Per the official answer: Salbardi–Amravati, Sav–Raigad, Vajreshwari–Thane, Changdev–Jalgaon — code (iv), (iii), (ii), (i). If your district list differs slightly, defer to the official answer for this item.

subject: Geography
question: Which district is largest and smallest in terms of geographical area in Aurangabad administrative division?
explanation: On this one, option B is correct. Within the Aurangabad administrative division, Beed is the largest district by area and Hingoli the smallest — the pair the official answer selects.

subject: Geography
question: In which mountain range of Maharashtra 'Asthamba Peak' is located?
explanation: Go with option C. Asthamba peak (about 1,325 m) stands in the Satpuda range at Nandurbar — not in the Sahyadri, Harishchandra or Mahadev sub-ranges of western Maharashtra.

subject: Geography
question: How many districts of Maharashtra have borders with state of Karnataka?
explanation: Pick option C. Seven Maharashtra districts touch Karnataka: Nanded, Latur, Osmanabad (Dharashiv), Solapur, Sangli, Kolhapur and Sindhudurg — a standard border-count fact for MPSC maps.

subject: General Studies
question: One inch air pressure means how much?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. One inch of mercury column equals roughly 33.86 millibars, rounded to 34 mb in exam keys — not the smaller values in options A and B.

subject: General Studies
question: Which city/cities in Maharashtra Mumbai-Agra highway does not pass through? (a) Amalner (b) Daund (c) Nashik (d) Dhule
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. The Mumbai–Agra highway (NH 3 corridor) runs through Nashik and Dhule in north Maharashtra, but it does not pass Amalner or Daund — Amalner sits on a Dhule–Jalgaon branch route and Daund lies on the Pune–Mumbai line. Only (a) and (b) are off the main Agra road.

subject: Geography
question: Observe the following statements: (a) The existence of jet streams in 30° to 40° North latitudes belt is responsible for blowing of Monsoon winds in India. (b) The Vast continental area of India is responsible for blowing of Monsoon winds.
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. The subtropical westerly jet over the 30°–40° N belt shifts north in summer and helps pull the monsoon trough inland, while India's huge landmass heats up faster than the surrounding oceans and builds the low-pressure engine that draws in moist winds. Both mechanisms work together in standard monsoon theory.

subject: General Studies
question: The first railway to run on electricity in Maharashtra _______.
explanation: The right pick is option B. India's first electric train service started on 3 February 1925 between Bombay (Mumbai) and Kurla on the Harbour line — that is the landmark date for Maharashtra. Byculla–Thane and Dadar–Borivali sections were electrified in later phases, not as the inaugural run.

subject: Geography
question: Nannaj Sanctuary in Solapur district is famous for which bird?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Nannaj Bird Sanctuary near Solapur is a stronghold of the Great Indian Bustard, locally called Maldhok — one of the rarest grassland birds in India. Peacocks and flamingos draw tourists elsewhere; this reserve is bustard country.

subject: Geography
question: The Jyotiba Mountain in Kolhapur district is recognised as _______. (a) Wadi Ratnagiri (b) Karvir (c) Panhala (d) The hill of Kedareshwar
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Jyotiba hill in Kolhapur district is traditionally known as Wadi Ratnagiri — the sacred hill of the Jyotiba temple. Karvir is the old name for Kolhapur town, Panhala is a separate fort-hill, and Kedareshwar labels another shrine, not this peak.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following is not the reason for Population Explosion in India? (a) Illiteracy (b) The Universalization of Marriage (c) Joint Family System (d) Upliftment in Life Style
explanation: Go with option D. Illiteracy, early universal marriage, and the joint-family norm all push larger family sizes and faster population growth. Rising lifestyle and education usually delay marriage and cut fertility — so upliftment in lifestyle is not a driver of population explosion.

subject: Economy
question: Repo rate is the rate at _______. (1) Commercial banks lend to public (2) The rate which is charged for Government lending (3) R.B.I. lends to commercial banks (4) The rate is charged on saving deposits with commercial banks
explanation: On this one, option C is correct. Repo (repurchase) rate is the short-term lending rate at which the RBI supplies funds to commercial banks against government securities — it is the headline policy rate, not the rate banks charge the public or pay on savings deposits.

subject: General Studies
question: When was the FRBM Act brought into effect?
explanation: Pick option D. Parliament passed the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act in 2003, and its operational provisions took effect from 5 July 2004 — that notification date is what MPSC keys. January 2000 and December 2003 are near-miss distractors around the rollout.

subject: General Studies
question: On July 19, 1969 fourteen commercial banks with deposits worth ₹ _______ or more were nationalised.
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. On 19 July 1969 the Union government nationalised fourteen major commercial banks whose deposits stood at ₹50 crore or more — the threshold written in every banking-history note. ₹75 crore and ₹100 crore are scaled-up distractors.

subject: Geography
question: Consider the following statements: (a) The population density of India in 2011 was 382 per sq. km. (b) As per the census 2011, the literacy rate in the country is 73.0 percent. (c) The sex ratio in the country has always remained favourable to females. Which of the statement/s given above is/are incorrect?
explanation: The right pick is option B. Census 2011 did put India's density at 382 per sq km and overall literacy at about 73% — those figures check out. Only Statement (c) is incorrect: India's sex ratio has long been male-heavy (fewer females per 1,000 males), not continuously favourable to females.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following is the department of Public Finance? (a) Public Expenditure (b) Public Revenue (c) Public Debt (d) Public Health Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Public finance covers how the government raises money (public revenue), spends it (public expenditure), and handles borrowing (public debt). Public health is a programme sector, not a branch of public-finance theory — so (a), (b), and (c) fit, not (d).

subject: General Studies
question: Credit Authorisation Scheme was introduced in _______.
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. RBI introduced the Credit Authorisation Scheme in November 1965 to vet large bank advances during the credit-squeeze era — before later liberalisation. The 1979, 1980, and 1982 dates belong to other monetary reforms.

subject: General Studies
question: Money Market faces shortage of funds due to:
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. When household and corporate saving stays low, the money market — the market for short-term funds — cannot meet the demand for working capital and trade credit. Growing cash demand and an unorganised sector add friction, but inadequate saving is the textbook root cause here.

subject: General Studies
question: Capital Receipt of State Government includes _______. (a) Market loans (b) Borrowing from Central Government (c) Small Saving of the public and provident fund contribution (d) G.S.T. share from Central Government Which of the above option is correct?
explanation: On this one, option C is correct. State capital receipts are borrowings and similar inflows: market loans (a), loans from the Centre (b), and small savings plus provident-fund flows (c). GST devolution from the Union is a revenue receipt — a tax share — not capital receipt, so (d) drops out.

subject: General Studies
question: Public Expenditure of any Government shows following trend:
explanation: Go with option B. As economies develop, governments take on welfare, defence, infrastructure, and subsidy bills — so public expenditure almost everywhere shows a long-run rising trend, not a flat, falling, or purely random path.

subject: Economy
question: Which Committee was appointed in 2011-2012 to re-examine the issue of poverty?
explanation: Pick option D. The C. Rangarajan Committee (2011–12) was asked to revisit poverty-line estimation after the Tendulkar line drew criticism — it recommended higher rural and urban poverty thresholds. Lakdawala and Chakravarty belong to earlier poverty-measurement exercises.

subject: General Studies
question: How much calories does a rural Indian man need from his daily diet?
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Planning-Commission poverty norms used 2,400 kilocalories per day for a rural adult man as the minimum energy requirement — 2,000 is closer to sedentary urban norms, and 2,500–2,750 are upper-band distractors.

subject: General Studies
question: By which financial institution, monetary policy is implemented in India?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Monetary policy — repo, bank rate, CRR, SLR, open-market operations — is formulated and executed by the Reserve Bank of India. LIC, UTI, and co-operative banks are financial intermediaries, not the nation's monetary authority.

subject: General Studies
question: National Oilseeds Development Project (NODP) was launched in the year _______.
explanation: The right pick is option C. The National Oilseeds Development Project (NODP) was launched in 1985–86 to expand area, productivity, and processing for oilseeds under the Technology Mission framework. The 1980–81 and 1989–90 windows are year-shift distractors.

subject: Economy
question: Consider the following statements: (a) Reserve Bank of India use the Dear Money Policy during the period of inflation. (b) Reserve Bank of India use the Cheap Money Policy during the period of depression. (c) The R.B.I. started with a Cheap Money Policy with a Bank rate of 3% in 1951. Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Dear money (tighter, costlier credit) fights inflation; cheap money (lower bank rate, easier credit) supports recovery in a depression — and RBI did pursue a cheap-money phase with a 3% bank rate around 1951. All three statements match standard RBI history.

subject: General Studies
question: _______ are used to know the speed of any vehicle.
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Speedometers and similar gauges use eddy currents — when a rotating magnet moves near a metal disc, induced eddy currents create a drag proportional to speed, and the dial reads that effect. Ordinary conduction or bare magnetic induction alone does not drive the meter.

subject: General Studies
question: Whenever there is a relative motion between a source of sound and an observer, there is apparent change in Frequency of a sound emitted by a source and as heard by the observer. This is called _______.
explanation: On this one, option C is correct. When a sound source and observer move relative to each other, the heard frequency shifts — higher on approach, lower on receding. That is the Doppler effect; Huygens, Joule, and Raman describe diffraction, heating, and scattering, not motion-induced pitch change.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following element was responsible for Minamata epidemic caused in Japan?
explanation: Go with option D. The Minamata disaster in Japan (1950s–60s) came from industrial mercury (Hg) dumped into Minamata Bay, which biomagnified through fish and caused severe neurological disease. Gold (Au), platinum (Pt), and silver (Ag) were not the toxic agents in that epidemic.

subject: General Studies
question: Phosphorous pentachloride formed by _______ hybridisation.
explanation: Pick option D. Phosphorus in PCl₅ forms five σ-bonds with no lone pair on the central atom — trigonal bipyramidal geometry — so the hybridisation is sp³d. sp²d and sp²d² under-count bond directions; sp³d² fits octahedral six-coordinate molecules such as SF₆, not PCl₅.

subject: General Studies
question: If the valence shell of an element has only one electron having the following set of quantum numbers: n = 2, l = 0, m = 0, s = +1/2, then the element is _______.
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. n = 2, l = 0, m = 0, s = +½ describes a 2s electron; with only one valence electron that configuration belongs to lithium (1s² 2s¹).

subject: General Studies
question: In heteroneresis the gonads are developed in the posterior part of the body. These gonads bearing segments are called:
explanation: The right pick is option A. In heteronereis the posterior, gonad-bearing swimming segments formed during reproduction are called epitokes; the anterior non-reproductive part is the atoke.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the following: (a) Salamander → (i) Poikilothermic (b) Duckbilled Platypus → (ii) Sanguivorous (c) Leech → (iii) Asymmetrical (d) Paramecium → (iv) Egg laying mammal
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Salamander is poikilothermic, duck-billed platypus is an egg-laying mammal, leech is sanguivorous, and Paramecium shows asymmetry — giving (i), (iv), (ii), (iii).

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following fish belongs to class Osteichthyes?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Catla is a bony fish (class Osteichthyes); shark, sting ray and electric ray belong to cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes).

subject: General Studies
question: _______ insecticide is present in neem plant. (a) DDT (b) Azadirachtin (c) Aldrin (d) B.H.C. Which of the option/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Neem's natural insecticidal compound is azadirachtin — not DDT, aldrin or BHC, which are synthetic organochlorines.

subject: General Studies
question: A plant that does not produce fruit is called _______. (a) acarpous (b) fertile (c) apocarpus (d) parthenocarpus
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Acarpous means a plant that does not set fruit; fertile, apocarpous and parthenocarpic describe other reproductive conditions.

subject: Science
question: The search for effective Malarial Vaccine is hampered due to the fact that:

options.A: Plasmodium lives inside cells hidden from immune response
options.C: Plasmodium requires two hosts to complete life cycle

explanation: The right pick is option D. Vaccine development against malaria is hard because Plasmodium hides inside host cells and also switches its surface antigens — both hurdles apply.

subject: General Studies
question: Consider the following statements: Statement I: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a microbial pesticide. Statement II: Beaveria bassiana is a fungus used as a pesticide.

options.A: Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
options.B: Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct

explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Bacillus thuringiensis is a bacterial bio-pesticide, and Beauveria bassiana is a fungus used similarly — both statements hold.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following WBC type has lowest percentage in blood of healthy human?
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Among normal WBC types, basophils form the smallest fraction (well under 1%), below lymphocytes, monocytes and eosinophils.

subject: Science
question: How does Insulin reduces blood glucose? (a) Promoting uptake of glucose (b) Glycogen formation (c) Protein synthesis (d) Fat storage
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting cellular uptake, glycogen synthesis, protein synthesis and fat storage — all four routes count.

subject: General Studies
question: According to the available data, quantum of pollution caused by various categories of vehicles on the road of certain city reveals that the private four wheeler vehicles cause the maximum pollution, this is followed by the pollution caused by the buses, the trucks and finally the two wheelers. (a) The number of two wheelers is less than the number of four wheelers plying on the city roads. (b) Pollution caused by a single private vehicle would be more than the pollution caused by any single bus.
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Total pollution by vehicle category depends on fleet size and per-trip emissions together — you cannot infer either vehicle counts or per-vehicle pollution from totals alone.

subject: General Studies
question: A person walks along a road having lamp post at regular intervals. He took 6 minutes to walk from the first to fourth lamp post. At which lamp post would the person be if he walked continuously at a constant rate for 20 minutes?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. First to fourth post spans three equal gaps in 6 minutes, so one gap takes 2 minutes; 20 minutes covers ten gaps from the start — the 11th lamp post.

subject: General Studies
question: Ashok jumped higher than Mohan but not higher than Chetan. Naresh jumped higher than Krishna but not as high as that of Mohan. Then what is the correct descending order of players considering their jump?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Chetan > Ashok > Mohan from the first clue, and Mohan > Naresh > Krishna from the second — full order: Chetan, Ashok, Mohan, Naresh, Krishna.

subject: Science
question: [Passage based] There is an increased demand for fish as it is a good source of protein. About 70% of world's marine fish stocks are now overfished. Aquaculture is continuously expanded but it is necessary to manage environmental risks. For this the aquaculture sector needs to devise effective and environment friendly methods. Select the most appropriate conclusion:

options.A: People should adopt total vegan diet for avoiding environmental problems.
options.B: Aquaculture of predator fishes should be banned till other environment friendly devise is designed for rearing them.
options.C: People should consume freshwater fish varieties to avoid pressure on oceans.
options.D: The farming of only certain kind of varieties is damaging the biodiversity of ecosystems.

explanation: The right pick is option B. The passage stresses managing aquaculture's environmental risks; banning predator-fish farming until safer rearing methods exist follows that logic most closely.

subject: General Studies
question: Some persons are sitting on a bench. V is sitting next to An and S is next to G. G is not sitting with Aj. Aj is on the left end of the bench and S is in second position from right hand end. V is on the right side of An and to the right side of Aj. V and S are sitting together. If G and V exchange their positions select the statement that is not true.

options.A: Positions cannot be ascertained as the direction they face is not known.
options.D: An occupies the second position from one of the end.

explanation: The examiner has marked option A. With Aj at the left end and the other conditions, the row fixes as Aj–An–V–S–G; after G and V swap, positions are known — so saying they 'cannot be ascertained' is the false statement.

subject: General Studies
question: Given below are 5 statements followed by options composed of 3 statements put together in a specific order. Choose the option that indicates logically valid argument. (a) Some vehicles are not hazardous to the environment. (b) Vehicular traffic leads to emission of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases. (c) Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are hazardous to the environment. (d) Some vehicular traffic does not emit Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases. (e) Vehicular traffic is hazardous to the environment.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Greenhouse gases harm the environment (c); vehicular traffic emits them (b); therefore traffic is environmentally hazardous (e) — a valid chain in that order.

subject: General Studies
question: If 10 people can do a piece of work in 5 days, working 2 hours a day, how long will 2 people take to do the same work, working 5 hours a day?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Total work = 10 × 5 × 2 = 100 person-hours; two workers at 5 hours/day supply 10 person-hours daily, so 100 ÷ 10 = 10 days.

subject: Reasoning
question: The average age of three person is 60 years. Their ages are in the ratio of 2 : 3 : 4. What is the difference between the ages of the youngest and the eldest person?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Ages in ratio 2: 3: 4 with average 60 give 40, 60 and 80 years — the youngest–eldest gap is 40 years.

subject: Reasoning
question: Replace the question mark (?) by an appropriate alternative in the following series: 32, 33, 37, 46, 62, ___?___
explanation: The right pick is option B. Successive gaps are +1, +4, +9, +16 (squares of 1–4); the next add-on is +25, so 62 + 25 = 87.

subject: General Studies
question: A street vendor sold 2 dolls more than half the number of dolls she has on one day. The next day she sold 2 dolls less than half of the remaining dolls available with her. If she was left with 26 dolls. Select the number of dolls she did initially have.
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. If she started with 100 dolls, day-one sale leaves 48; day-two sale (half minus 2 of 48) leaves exactly 26 — working backwards confirms 100.

subject: Reasoning
question: If the ratio of two numbers is 3 : 4 and the sum of their squares is 400, then which are these numbers?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Numbers 3k and 4k give 9k² + 16k² = 25k² = 400, so k = 4 and the pair is 12 and 16.

subject: General Studies
question: Neha's salary was first reduced by 10% and then increased by 30% due to upturn. So what percent increase in original salary?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. A 10% cut then 30% rise on the reduced salary gives 0.9 × 1.3 = 1.17, i.e. a net 17% increase over the original.

subject: General Studies
question: The difference between the simple and compound interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹ 750. What is the sum?
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. For 2 years the compound-minus-simple interest gap equals P × (R/100)² = P × 0.01; with ₹750 difference, P = ₹75,000.

subject: General Studies
question: The value of 1/(856×592) + 1/(856×264) − 1/(592×264) is _______.
explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Factor the sum: 1/(856×592) + 1/(856×264) − 1/(592×264) simplifies to 856/(856×592×264) − 856/(856×592×264) = 0.

subject: General Studies
question: Soma moves 10 km to East and then turns to South and moves 2 km. He again turn East and walks 2 km. After this, he turns to North and walks 7 km. Then the distance from his starting point to the present point is _______.

options.D: Can not be determined from the given data

explanation: The right pick is option A. Net displacement is 12 km east and 5 km north from the start (√(12² + 5²) = 13 km), using east–west and north–south legs as given.

subject: General Studies
question: 2021 च्या ब्रिक्स फिल्म फेस्टिवल मध्ये खालीलपैकी कोणाला उत्कृष्ट पुरुष अभिनेत्याचा पुरस्कार मिळाला?
explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय D येतो. Dhanush यांना 'Asuran' साठी BRICS Film Festival 2021 मध्ये Best Actor (Male) पुरस्कार मिळाला. Nawazuddin, Akshay Kumar, Pankaj Tripathi त्या वर्षी भारतीय चित्रपटात मोठे नाव होते, पण हा विशिष्ट पुरस्कार त्यांना नव्हता.

subject: Economy
question: 2022 सालचे प्रतिष्ठित बोल्ट्झमन पदक प्राप्त करणारे पहिले भारतीय भौतिकशास्त्रज्ञ कोण आहेत?
explanation: थेट उत्तर — पर्याय A. Professor Deepak Dhar 2022 मध्ये Boltzmann Medal मिळवणारे पहिले भारतीय भौतिकशास्त्रज्ञ झाले — IUPAP ने statistical physics मध्ये उत्कृष्ट योगदानासाठी. Ashok Kumar Barua, Bimla Buti, D.D. Bhawalkar नामवंत भौतिकशास्त्रज्ञ, पण Boltzmann Medal विजेते नाहीत.
